question: Can a transformer whose attention cost grows linearly with length process long documents, and serve as a drop-in replacement for self-attention in pretrained models on document-level tasks?
hypothesis: A combination of sliding-window local attention and task-motivated global attention, continued-pretrained from RoBERTa, will beat chunked RoBERTa baselines on long-document tasks.
contributions: Longformer attention: sliding window, dilated sliding window and task-motivated global attention, linear in sequence length
State-of-the-art character-level LM on text8 and enwik8 (small models)
Pretrained Longformer (continued from RoBERTa, 4,096 tokens) that beats RoBERTa on long-document tasks and sets SOTA on WikiHop and TriviaQA
Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED) for long-document seq2seq, evaluated on arXiv summarization

method.summary: Self-attention is sparsified to a fixed-size sliding window (optionally dilated on some heads) plus symmetric global attention on a few task-chosen tokens, with separate Q/K/V projections for global attention. Evaluated by training character-level LMs from scratch with a staged window/length schedule, by continuing MLM pretraining from RoBERTa with copied position embeddings to 4,096 tokens then finetuning on six tasks, and by LED initialised from BART with 16K positions.

models.name: Longformer char-LM small
models.architecture: decoder transformer, Transformer-XL code with memory disabled, relative sinusoidal position embeddings, pre-layernorm, GeLU, dilated sliding window

models.name: Longformer-base / Longformer-large
models.architecture: RoBERTa with sliding-window attention, window 512, plus global attention with extra projections
models.init_from: RoBERTa released checkpoint, position embeddings copied 8 times from 512 to 4,096

other.dilation: not used in pretrained model; footnote 6 says it hurt performance

models.name: RoBERTa-base / large
models.architecture: full self-attention; long inputs split into longest possible 512 segments, activations concatenated

models.name: LED-base / LED-large
models.architecture: BART encoder-decoder, encoder uses Longformer local+global attention, decoder full attention
models.init_from: BART, position embeddings copied 16 times from 1K to 16K
models.layers: 6 (base) and 12 (large) in both encoder and decoder

training.objective: MLM continued from RoBERTa (main pretraining); autoregressive char LM for text8/enwik8; task losses for finetuning; teacher forcing for LED
training.optimizer: MLM pretraining: not stated beyond 'rest same as RoBERTa'; char-LM AdamW; finetuning Adam
training.lr_schedule: MLM pretraining: linear warmup then power 3 polynomial decay
training.precision: char-LM mixed precision fp16/fp32 with apex, attention kept in fp32
training.hardware: char-LM: 48GB RTX8000; MLM pretraining hardware not stated
training.compute: char-LM small 4 RTX8000 for 16 days; large 8 RTX8000 for 13 days
training.seeds: Hyperpartisan: mean F1 across five seeds; otherwise not stated

other.char_lm_phases: 5 phases; window and sequence length doubled and LR halved each phase; seq len 2,048 to 23,040; phase 1 windows 32 (bottom) to 8,192 (top), phase 5 bottom window 512; phase 1 LR 0.00025; batch per phase 32,32,16,16,16; steps per phase small 430K,50k,50k,35k,5k and large 350K,25k,10k,5k,5k; warmup 10% of phase steps max 10K; constant LR within a phase
other.frozen_variant: pretraining with all RoBERTa weights frozen and only new position embeddings trained gave MLM BPC 1.850 (base)
other.wikihop_finetune: Adam, 15 epochs, LR 3e-5, warmup 200, batch 32; dev accuracy checked every 250 updates, max reported; single RTX8000, about a day for 5 epochs of base
other.triviaqa_finetune: Adam, 5 epochs, LR 3e-5, warmup 1000, batch 32; 32GB V100, small 1 day on 4 GPUs, large 1 day on 8 GPUs
other.hotpotqa_finetune: Adam, 5 epochs, LR 5e-5 (Table 14; text says 3e-5 and 5 epochs best), warmup 1000, batch 32; RTX8000, about half a day per epoch on 4 GPUs
other.coref_finetune: RoBERTa LR 1e-5, task LR 1e-4 for Longformer-base; sequence length 384 for RoBERTa-base and 4,096 for Longformer-base; about 10 hours on one GPU
other.classification_finetune: Adam, batch 32, LR 3e-5, 15 epochs, warmup 0.1 of steps; single RTX8000
other.hyperparameter_search: grid searches kept small and identical for RoBERTa-base and Longformer-base

inference.decoding: LED: beam search (width not stated); HotpotQA evidence: constrained decoding so evidence sentences come from exactly two paragraphs
inference.samples: single run per config except Hyperpartisan (five seeds); Longformer-large TriviaQA trained once

other.char_lm_eval: sequences of 32,256 with step 512, report BPC on last 512 tokens

limits: Authors concede BigBird later improved leaderboard results, with a possible confound of 16x more pretraining compute.
Dilation is used only in the char-LM; it hurt in the pretrained RoBERTa-based model (footnote 6).
Ablation ordering at 150K steps may not match end-of-training ordering (footnote 4).
Global attention locations are task-specific and hand-chosen.
Longformer-large WikiHop sees only the first 4,096 tokens due to memory.
Hyperparameter searches were minimal; the large-model results are single runs.
Pretraining hardware and total compute for the MLM stage are not stated.
LED not pretrained; authors expect gains from pretraining.
Table 14 lists HotpotQA LR 5e-5 while the text says 3e-5 worked best.

terms.definition: Given a fixed window size w, each token attends to 1/2 w tokens on each side; cost O(n x w).
The window has gaps of size dilation d; receptive field is l x d x w.
A token with global attention attends to all tokens and all tokens attend to it, applied to a few pre-selected locations.
